def lis(a)
  tails=[]
  a.each do |x|
    lo=0;hi=tails.length
    while lo<hi
      mid=(lo+hi)/2
      tails[mid]<x ? lo=mid+1 : hi=mid
    end
    tails[lo]=x
  end
  tails.length
end

reference:
def trap_rain(h)
  return 0 if h.empty?
  l=0;r=h.length-1;lm=0;rm=0;res=0
  while l<r
    if h[l]<h[r]
      h[l]>=lm ? lm=h[l] : res+=lm-h[l]; l+=1
    else
      h[r]>=rm ? rm=h[r] : res+=rm-h[r]; r-=1
    end
  end
  res
end

prompt: Define `spiral(m)` returning the elements of 2D array m in clockwise spiral order.
reference:
def spiral(m)
  res=[];return res if m.empty?
  top=0;bot=m.length-1;left=0;right=m[0].length-1
  while top<=bot && left<=right
    (left..right).each{|c| res<<m[top][c]};top+=1
    (top..bot).each{|r| res<<m[r][right]};right-=1
    (right.downto(left){|c| res<<m[bot][c]};bot-=1) if top<=bot
    (bot.downto(top){|r| res<<m[r][left]};left+=1) if left<=right
  end
  res
end

def n_queens(n)
  count=0;cols={};d1={};d2={}

    (count+=1;return) if r==n
    (0...n).each do |c|
      next if cols[c]||d1[r-c]||d2[r+c]
      cols[c]=d1[r-c]=d2[r+c]=true
      solve.call(r+1)
      cols[c]=d1[r-c]=d2[r+c]=false
    end
  end

prompt: Define `regex_match(s,p)` implementing regex matching where '.' matches any single char and '*' matches zero or more of the preceding element. Match must cover the ENTIRE string.
reference:
def regex_match(s,p)
  memo={}
  dp=lambda do |i,j|
    k=[i,j];return memo[k] if memo.key?(k)
    res = if j==p.length
      i==s.length
    else
      first=i<s.length && (p[j]==s[i]||p[j]==".")
      if j+1<p.length && p[j+1]=="*"
        dp.call(i,j+2)||(first&&dp.call(i+1,j))
      else
        first&&dp.call(i+1,j+1)
      end
    end
    memo[k]=res
  end
  dp.call(0,0)
end

def combination_sum(cands,target)
  res=0;c=cands.sort
  dfs=lambda do |start,remain|
    (res+=1;return) if remain==0
    (start...c.length).each do |i|
      break if c[i]>remain
      dfs.call(i,remain-c[i])
    end
  end

end

class Version
  include Comparable
  attr_reader :parts
  def initialize(s); @parts=s.split(".").map(&:to_i); end
  def <=>(o)
    n=[@parts.length,o.parts.length].max

      c=(@parts[i]||0)<=>(o.parts[i]||0)

    end
    0
  end
end

prompt: Define `eval_expr(s)` evaluating an arithmetic expression string with non-negative integers, + - * / (integer division) and parentheses, honoring precedence. Do NOT use Kernel#eval.
reference:
def eval_expr(s)
  tokens=s.scan(/\d+|[()+\-*\/]/)
  pos=0
  peek=->{ tokens[pos] }
  nextt=->{ t=tokens[pos];pos+=1;t }
  parse_expr=nil;parse_term=nil;parse_factor=nil
  parse_factor=lambda do
    if peek.call=="("
      nextt.call;v=parse_expr.call;nextt.call;v
    else
      nextt.call.to_i
    end
  end
  parse_term=lambda do
    v=parse_factor.call
    while ["*","/"].include?(peek.call)
      op=nextt.call;r=parse_factor.call
      v = op=="*" ? v*r : v/r
    end
    v
  end
  parse_expr=lambda do
    v=parse_term.call
    while ["+","-"].include?(peek.call)
      op=nextt.call;r=parse_term.call
      v = op=="+" ? v+r : v-r
    end
    v
  end
  parse_expr.call
end

def longest_palindrome_len(s)
  return 0 if s.empty?

    while l>=0 && r<s.length && s[l]==s[r]; l-=1;r+=1; end

prompt: Define `longest_inc_path(grid)` = length of the longest strictly increasing path in a 2D integer grid, moving up/down/left/right.
reference:
def longest_inc_path(grid)
  return 0 if grid.empty? || grid[0].empty?
  rows=grid.length; cols=grid[0].length
  memo=Array.new(rows){Array.new(cols,0)}
  dfs=lambda do |r,c|
    return memo[r][c] if memo[r][c]>0
    best=1
    [[1,0],[-1,0],[0,1],[0,-1]].each do |dr,dc|
      nr=r+dr; nc=c+dc
      if nr>=0 && nr<rows && nc>=0 && nc<cols && grid[nr][nc]>grid[r][c]
        best=[best,1+dfs.call(nr,nc)].max
      end
    end
    memo[r][c]=best
  end
  best=0
  (0...rows).each{|r| (0...cols).each{|c| best=[best,dfs.call(r,c)].max}}
  best
end

prompt: Define `word_ladder(begin_word,end_word,word_list)` = length (word count) of the shortest transformation sequence from begin_word to end_word changing one letter at a time, each intermediate word must be in word_list; return 0 if impossible.
reference:
def word_ladder(begin_word, end_word, word_list)
  dict = word_list.to_a
  return 0 unless dict.include?(end_word)
  visited = {begin_word=>true}
  queue = [[begin_word,1]]
  until queue.empty?
    word, dist = queue.shift
    return dist if word==end_word
    ('a'..'z').each do |ch|
      (0...word.length).each do |i|
        next_word = word.dup
        next_word[i]=ch
        if dict.include?(next_word) && !visited[next_word]
          visited[next_word]=true
          queue<<[next_word,dist+1]
        end
      end
    end
  end
  0
end

reference:
def max_rect_hist(heights)
  stack=[]
  max_area=0
  heights_ext = heights + [0]
  heights_ext.each_with_index do |h,i|
    while !stack.empty? && heights_ext[stack.last]>=h
      top=stack.pop
      height=heights_ext[top]
      width = stack.empty? ? i : i-stack.last-1
      max_area=[max_area,height*width].max
    end
    stack<<i
  end
  max_area
end

reference:
def sliding_max(a,k)
  return [] if a.empty? || k<=0
  deque=[]
  res=[]
  a.each_with_index do |x,i|
    deque.shift while !deque.empty? && deque.first <= i-k
    deque.pop while !deque.empty? && a[deque.last] <= x
    deque<<i
    res<<a[deque.first] if i>=k-1
  end
  res
end

prompt: Define `min_window_substr(s,t)` = the smallest substring of s containing every character of t (with multiplicity); return "" if no such window exists.
reference:
def min_window_substr(s,t)
  return "" if s.empty? || t.empty?
  need=Hash.new(0)
  t.each_char{|c| need[c]+=1}
  required=need.size
  formed=0
  window=Hash.new(0)
  l=0
  best_len=Float::INFINITY; best_l=nil; best_r=nil
  s.each_char.with_index do |c,r|
    window[c]+=1
    if need.key?(c) && window[c]==need[c]
      formed+=1
    end
    while l<=r && formed==required
      if r-l+1<best_len
        best_len=r-l+1; best_l=l; best_r=r
      end
      c2=s[l]
      window[c2]-=1
      if need.key?(c2) && window[c2]<need[c2]
        formed-=1
      end
      l+=1
    end
  end
  best_len==Float::INFINITY ? "" : s[best_l..best_r]
end

prompt: Define `word_search(board,word)` returning true iff word can be constructed from adjacent (up/down/left/right, non-reused) cells of the 2D char grid board.
reference:
def word_search(board, word)
  return true if word.empty?
  rows=board.length; cols=board[0].length
  visited=Array.new(rows){Array.new(cols,false)}
  dfs=lambda do |r,c,idx|
    return true if idx==word.length
    return false if r<0||r>=rows||c<0||c>=cols||visited[r][c]||board[r][c]!=word[idx]
    visited[r][c]=true
    found = dfs.call(r+1,c,idx+1)||dfs.call(r-1,c,idx+1)||dfs.call(r,c+1,idx+1)||dfs.call(r,c-1,idx+1)
    visited[r][c]=false
    found
  end
  (0...rows).each do |r|
    (0...cols).each do |c|
      return true if dfs.call(r,c,0)
    end
  end
  false
end

def partition_equal(a)
  total=a.sum
  return false if total.odd?
  target=total/2
  dp=Array.new(target+1,false)
  dp[0]=true
  a.each do |num|
    next if num>target
    target.downto(num) do |j|
      dp[j] ||= dp[j-num]
    end
  end
  dp[target]
end

def maximal_square(matrix)
  return 0 if matrix.empty? || matrix[0].empty?
  rows=matrix.length; cols=matrix[0].length
  dp=Array.new(rows+1){Array.new(cols+1,0)}
  best=0
  (1..rows).each do |i|
    (1..cols).each do |j|
      if matrix[i-1][j-1]==1
        dp[i][j]=[dp[i-1][j],dp[i][j-1],dp[i-1][j-1]].min+1
        best=[best,dp[i][j]].max
      end
    end
  end
  best*best
end

prompt: Define `multiply_strings(a,b)` multiplying two non-negative base-10 integers given as digit strings, returning the product as a string with no leading zeros (except "0" itself). Do not use Integer#* on the parsed whole numbers.
reference:
def multiply_strings(a,b)
  return "0" if a=="0"||b=="0"
  m=a.length; n=b.length
  res=Array.new(m+n,0)
  (m-1).downto(0) do |i|
    (n-1).downto(0) do |j|
      mul=(a[i].to_i)*(b[j].to_i)
      p1=i+j; p2=i+j+1
      total=mul+res[p2]
      res[p2]=total%10
      res[p1]+=total/10
    end
  end
  s=res.join
  s=s.sub(/\A0+(?=\d)/,"")
  s
end

raise unless multiply_strings("123","456")=="56088"

prompt: Define `find_duplicate(a)` for an array of n+1 integers each in 1..n with exactly one value duplicated (possibly multiple times); return the duplicated value using Floyd's cycle detection (O(n) time, O(1) extra space; do not sort or use a Set/Hash).
reference:
def find_duplicate(a)
  slow=a[0]; fast=a[0]
  loop do
    slow=a[slow]
    fast=a[a[fast]]
    break if slow==fast
  end
  slow2=a[0]
  until slow2==slow
    slow2=a[slow2]
    slow=a[slow]
  end
  slow
end

prompt: Define `next_permutation(a)` returning a NEW array holding the next lexicographically greater permutation of a; if a is the highest permutation, return the lowest (ascending sorted) permutation. Do not mutate a.
reference:
def next_permutation(a)
  arr=a.dup
  n=arr.length
  i=n-2
  i-=1 while i>=0 && arr[i]>=arr[i+1]
  if i>=0
    j=n-1
    j-=1 while arr[j]<=arr[i]
    arr[i],arr[j]=arr[j],arr[i]
  end
  lo=i+1; hi=n-1
  while lo<hi
    arr[lo],arr[hi]=arr[hi],arr[lo]
    lo+=1; hi-=1
  end
  arr
end

prompt: Define `binary_search_rotated(a,target)` doing an O(log n) search for target in an ascending array a that has been rotated at an unknown pivot (all values distinct); return the index of target, or -1 if absent.
reference:
def binary_search_rotated(a,target)
  lo=0; hi=a.length-1
  while lo<=hi
    mid=(lo+hi)/2
    return mid if a[mid]==target
    if a[lo]<=a[mid]
      if a[lo]<=target && target<a[mid]
        hi=mid-1
      else
        lo=mid+1
      end
    else
      if a[mid]<target && target<=a[hi]
        lo=mid+1
      else
        hi=mid-1
      end
    end
  end
  -1
end

prompt: Define a class `MinHeap` with `#push(x)` and `#pop` (removes and returns the minimum, nil if empty) and `#size`, implemented as a binary heap (not a sort-on-pop wrapper).
reference:
class MinHeap
  def initialize
    @data=[]
  end
  def push(x)
    @data<<x
    i=@data.length-1
    while i>0
      parent=(i-1)/2
      break if @data[parent]<=@data[i]
      @data[parent],@data[i]=@data[i],@data[parent]
      i=parent
    end
  end
  def pop
    return nil if @data.empty?
    top=@data[0]
    last=@data.pop
    unless @data.empty?
      @data[0]=last
      i=0
      loop do
        l=2*i+1; r=2*i+2; smallest=i
        smallest=l if l<@data.length && @data[l]<@data[smallest]
        smallest=r if r<@data.length && @data[r]<@data[smallest]
        break if smallest==i
        @data[i],@data[smallest]=@data[smallest],@data[i]
        i=smallest
      end
    end
    top
  end
  def size
    @data.length
  end
end

prompt: Define `matrix_chain_order(dims)` where dims has length n+1 and matrix i (1-indexed, i=1..n) has dimensions dims[i-1] x dims[i]; return the minimum number of scalar multiplications needed to compute the full chain product.
reference:
def matrix_chain_order(dims)
  n=dims.length-1
  return 0 if n<=1
  dp=Array.new(n+1){Array.new(n+1,0)}
  (2..n).each do |len|
    (1..(n-len+1)).each do |i|
      j=i+len-1
      dp[i][j]=Float::INFINITY
      (i...j).each do |k|
        cost=dp[i][k]+dp[k+1][j]+dims[i-1]*dims[k]*dims[j]
        dp[i][j]=cost if cost<dp[i][j]
      end
    end
  end
  dp[1][n]
end

prompt: Define `zigzag_convert(s,num_rows)` writing s in a zigzag pattern across num_rows rows (down then diagonally up, repeating) and returning the string read row by row.
reference:
def zigzag_convert(s, num_rows)
  return s if num_rows<=1
  rows=Array.new([num_rows,s.length].min){""}
  cur=0; going_down=false
  s.each_char do |c|
    rows[cur]+=c
    going_down = !going_down if cur==0 || cur==num_rows-1
    cur += going_down ? 1 : -1
  end
  rows.join
end

reference:
def merge_intervals(intervals)
  return [] if intervals.empty?
  sorted=intervals.sort_by{|iv| iv[0]}
  res=[sorted[0].dup]
  sorted[1..].each do |iv|
    last=res.last
    if iv[0]<=last[1]
      last[1]=[last[1],iv[1]].max
    else
      res<<iv.dup
    end
  end
  res
end

prompt: Define `decode_ways(s)` = number of ways to decode a digit string s into letters where '1'->'A' .. '26'->'Z' (a leading/standalone '0' has no mapping).
reference:
def decode_ways(s)
  return 0 if s.empty? || s[0]=="0"
  n=s.length
  dp=Array.new(n+1,0)
  dp[0]=1; dp[1]=1
  (2..n).each do |i|
    one=s[i-1,1].to_i
    two=s[i-2,2].to_i
    dp[i]=0
    dp[i]+=dp[i-1] if one.between?(1,9)
    dp[i]+=dp[i-2] if two.between?(10,26)
  end
  dp[n]
end

prompt: Define `jump_game_min(a)` = the minimum number of jumps needed to go from index 0 to the last index of array a, where a[i] is the maximum jump length from index i (input always guarantees the end is reachable).
reference:
def jump_game_min(a)
  n=a.length
  return 0 if n<=1
  jumps=0; cur_end=0; farthest=0
  (0...n-1).each do |i|
    farthest=[farthest,i+a[i]].max
    if i==cur_end
      jumps+=1
      cur_end=farthest
      break if cur_end>=n-1
    end
  end
  jumps
end

prompt: Define `count_islands(grid)` = the number of 4-directionally connected groups (islands) of 1-cells in a 0/1 integer grid.
reference:
def count_islands(grid)
  return 0 if grid.empty?
  rows=grid.length; cols=grid[0].length
  visited=Array.new(rows){Array.new(cols,false)}
  count=0
  (0...rows).each do |r|
    (0...cols).each do |c|
      if grid[r][c]==1 && !visited[r][c]
        count+=1
        stack=[[r,c]]
        visited[r][c]=true
        until stack.empty?
          cr,cc=stack.pop
          [[1,0],[-1,0],[0,1],[0,-1]].each do |dr,dc|
            nr=cr+dr; nc=cc+dc
            if nr>=0 && nr<rows && nc>=0 && nc<cols && grid[nr][nc]==1 && !visited[nr][nc]
              visited[nr][nc]=true
              stack<<[nr,nc]
            end
          end
        end
      end
    end
  end
  count
end

require 'set'
def longest_consecutive(a)
  set=Set.new(a)
  best=0
  set.each do |x|
    next if set.include?(x-1)
    len=1
    y=x
    while set.include?(y+1)
      y+=1
      len+=1
    end
    best=[best,len].max
  end
  best
end

Define a class `RationalNum` (constructed with integer numerator, denominator) that includes Comparable, auto-reduces via gcd (denominator kept positive), exposes `#num`/`#den`, defines `#+` returning a reduced RationalNum sum, and `#to_s` as "num/den".
reference:
class RationalNum
  include Comparable
  attr_reader :num, :den
  def initialize(n,d)
    g=n.gcd(d)
    g=1 if g==0
    sign = d<0 ? -1 : 1
    @num=sign*n/g
    @den=sign*d/g
  end
  def <=>(o)
    (@num*o.den)<=>(o.num*@den)
  end
  def +(o)
    RationalNum.new(@num*o.den+o.num*@den, @den*o.den)
  end
  def to_s
    "#{@num}/#{@den}"
  end
end
test:

raise unless RationalNum.new(1,3)<RationalNum.new(1,2)

raise unless r.to_s=="5/6"

def longest_common_prefix(strs)
  return "" if strs.empty?
  prefix=strs[0]
  strs[1..].each do |s|
    while !s.start_with?(prefix)
      prefix=prefix[0...-1]
      return "" if prefix.empty?
    end
  end
  prefix
end
